title: Tokyo, Japan: Cherry Blossoms, Omakase & Neon Nights
description: Six days immersed in Tokyo's electric energy — from late-blooming cherry blossoms in Shinjuku Gyoen to 3-Michelin-star omakase, volcanic onsen in Hakone, retro gaming in Akihabara, and golden hour above Shibuya Crossing. A trip that balances splurge-worthy moments with hidden local gems.

days.title: Arrival & Shinjuku After Dark
days.description: Land in Tokyo and dive straight into Shinjuku's neon-lit nightlife. Late cherry blossoms, smoky yakitori alleys, and tiny bars await.

activities.name: Arrive at Narita/Haneda Airport
activities.description: Pick up your Suica IC card at the airport for seamless transit. Take the Narita Express or Limousine Bus to Shinjuku — about 90 minutes. The iconic Lost in Translation hotel in Shinjuku. Stunning 52nd-floor views of the city skyline, impeccable service, and the legendary New York Bar upstairs. Worth the splurge for a couple's trip.

activities.name: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden
activities.description: If you arrive with daylight, walk to Shinjuku Gyoen (closes 6PM in April). Mid-April means late-blooming yaezakura cherry blossoms — the fluffy pink double-petal varieties are spectacular. Entry ¥500.

activities.name: Golden Gai Bar Crawl
activities.description: 200+ tiny bars crammed into 6 narrow alleys, each seating 5-8 people. Start at Bar Plastic Model (vintage toy decor) or Albatross (three floors of candlelit charm).

days.title: Temples, Old Tokyo & Asakusa Soul
days.description: Step back in time through Tokyo's oldest temple, a neighborhood that survived WWII, and bustling outdoor markets — ending with DIY okonomiyaki and Senso-ji lit up at night.

activities.name: Senso-ji Temple & Nakamise-dori
activities.description: Tokyo's oldest temple is magical at dawn before crowds arrive. Walk through the iconic Kaminarimon (Thunder Gate), browse Nakamise-dori for ningyo-yaki cakes and sensu fans.

activities.name: Yanaka District
activities.description: Take the subway to Nippori and wander Yanaka — Tokyo's old-town neighborhood that survived WWII bombing. Stroll Yanaka Ginza shopping street, visit Yanaka Cemetery (gorgeous with late cherry blossoms), and discover tiny galleries and cat statues everywhere.

activities.name: Ueno Park & Tokyo National Museum
activities.description: Walk through Ueno Park — check for lingering cherry blossoms around Shinobazu Pond. Then visit Tokyo National Museum, Japan's oldest and largest museum with samurai armor, ukiyo-e prints, and ancient ceramics. The buzzing outdoor market beneath the Yamanote Line tracks. Vendors shout deals on fresh seafood, dried fruits, sneakers, and street food. Try the fresh fruit mochi or a ¥500 seafood don.

activities.name: Senso-ji at Night
activities.description: Return to Senso-ji after dark — the pagoda and gate are illuminated and the crowds disappear. One of Tokyo's most photogenic moments. The contrast between the red lanterns and night sky is unforgettable.

days.title: Harajuku, Shibuya & the Omakase Splurge
days.description: From the serene forest of Meiji Shrine to Shibuya's electric crossing, cherry blossom petals on the Meguro River, and the meal of a lifetime at a 3-Michelin-star sushi counter.

activities.name: Meiji Shrine (Meiji Jingu)
activities.description: Walk through the towering torii gate into a 170-acre forest in the heart of Tokyo. The gravel path through ancient camphor trees is meditative. Check for traditional Shinto weddings on weekends.

activities.name: Harajuku & Takeshita Street
activities.description: From Meiji Shrine, exit onto Harajuku's famous Takeshita-dori. A kaleidoscope of kawaii fashion, crepe shops, and quirky boutiques. Visit the side streets (Cat Street, Ura-Harajuku) for independent designer shops and vintage finds.

activities.name: Shibuya Crossing & Shibuya Sky
activities.description: Experience the world's busiest pedestrian crossing, then head up Shibuya Scramble Square to Shibuya Sky — a 360° open-air observation deck on the 46th floor. The rooftop is incredible at golden hour. If late blooms remain, walk along the Meguro River from Nakameguro — 800+ cherry trees line both banks for nearly 4km. Even post-peak, the hanafubuki (petal blizzard) floating on the water is enchanting.

days.title: Hakone Day Trip — Onsen, Mountains & Mt. Fuji
days.description: Escape the city for volcanic valleys, a pirate ship cruise on a mountain lake, the iconic floating torii gate, and a private outdoor onsen surrounded by forest.

activities.name: Romancecar to Hakone
activities.description: Board the Odakyu Romancecar from Shinjuku Station — a sleek limited-express train with panoramic windows. The 85-minute ride is scenic and comfortable. An incredible sculpture garden set against mountain backdrops, featuring works by Picasso, Henry Moore, and Japanese artists. The foot onsen inside the museum is a fun surprise — bring a small towel.

activities.name: Hakone Ropeway & Owakudani
activities.description: Take the aerial ropeway over volcanic Owakudani valley — steaming sulfur vents and (on clear days) a jaw-dropping view of Mt. Fuji. At the top, eat the famous kuro-tamago (black eggs) boiled in sulfur springs.

activities.name: Lake Ashi Pirate Ship Cruise
activities.description: Descend from Owakudani to Togendai port and board one of the whimsical pirate ship replicas across Lake Ashi. On clear days, Mt. Fuji reflects in the lake — a postcard-perfect scene. The iconic red torii gate standing in Lake Ashi is one of Japan's most photographed spots. Walk the cedar-lined path to the shrine through ancient forest. Peaceful, spiritual, and absolutely stunning.

activities.name: Romancecar Back to Shinjuku
activities.description: Catch the evening Romancecar back to Shinjuku. The night ride is peaceful — you'll be onsen-relaxed and full of great food. Arrives around 9PM.

days.title: Digital Art, Retro Tokyo & Izakaya Night
days.description: The most eclectic day — from the freshest seafood breakfast to immersive digital art, retro gaming in Electric Town, indie vintage shopping, and an atmospheric izakaya crawl under the train tracks.

activities.name: teamLab Borderless (Azabudai Hills)
activities.description: The world's first digital art museum, relocated to Azabudai Hills in 2024. Immersive, boundary-less rooms of flowing light, waterfalls, and interactive art that responds to your movement. Allow 2-3 hours.

activities.name: Akihabara Electric Town
activities.description: Anime, manga, retro gaming, maid cafes — Akihabara is sensory overload in the best way. Browse Super Potato for retro games, Radio Kaikan for anime figures, and Don Quijote for wild souvenirs. Take the Keio Inokashira Line to Shimokita — Tokyo's indie neighborhood. New York Joe Exchange and Flamingo for vintage clothing, tiny live music venues, independent bookshops, and a bohemian vibe unlike anywhere else.

days.title: Ginza, Imperial Gardens & Farewell Tokyo
days.description: A graceful final day — leisurely brunch, the Emperor's serene gardens, Michelin-star tempura in Ginza, and a ceremonial matcha to close the chapter on an unforgettable trip.

activities.name: Imperial Palace East Gardens
activities.description: Free entry to the beautifully manicured gardens of the Emperor's residence. Wander through Ninomaru Garden with its iris beds, stone walls of the old Edo Castle, and peaceful lawns. A calm, reflective start to your last day.

activities.name: Ginza District
activities.description: Tokyo's upscale shopping boulevard. Browse the stunning Ginza Six (rooftop garden!), the Uniqlo flagship (12 floors), and Itoya stationery store — a paradise for pen lovers. Window shopping here is an experience itself.

activities.name: Souvenir Shopping
activities.description: Last-minute gifts — Tokyu Hands for beautifully designed Japanese goods, or Don Quijote for fun, quirky snacks. Pick up Tokyo Banana, matcha KitKats, and tenugui hand towels.

activities.name: Depart for Airport
activities.description: Head to Narita (90 min) or Haneda (30 min) for your flight. The Narita Express from Tokyo Station is most convenient for Narita.
